defaults.setup: Build the once-created exact candidate and inspect its npm tarballs, skills/contracts archives, manifest, checksums, SBOM, licenses, and dependency graph.
defaults.action: Run package and architecture gates against extracted candidate bytes without workspace imports.

rows.oracle: Tarballs expose exact root exports/bins, dependency direction, and no deep-import or third-party core compatibility claim.
Optional local artifact generation remains available without becoming an npm publication prerequisite.
All packages enforce Node ^24.0.0 ESM and every platform artifact contains no native addon, bundled runtime, browser, or install build.
Installed exact-version CLI operates an ordinary directory with none of the forbidden project metadata or services.
CLI/MCP tarballs contain shrinkwraps and explicit files, no lifecycle install scripts, and exact allowed dependency graphs.
Pinned installer and checksummed fallback copy immutable bytes only after approval and setup never bootstraps itself.
Every package, skill, contract, doc, evidence item, and manifest reports one exact full release version.
Version-policy fixtures classify patch, minor, and major changes exactly and reject incompatible contract drift on lower releases.
Compatibility gates inspect prior disk families and current/prior protocol families with the required migration and notice boundaries.
Stable and prerelease npm channels match policy while every public install reference pins exact SemVer.
One manual main workflow builds, packs, and publishes core, CLI, and MCP directly with OIDC and no ceremony inputs.
License-map inspection includes only local corpus paths and explicitly excludes hosted root/assets, brand, user content, and third-party works.
Every independent artifact contains its exact complete license/notices and copied-license inventory based on final bytes.
Normal pull request review and DCO sign-off apply without a second publication ceremony.
Packed npm tarballs contain the expected runtime files, lockstep dependencies, package metadata, and license material.
Optional platform qualification remains runnable independently and is not an npm publication input.
Support documentation records the deferred empty set without making host qualification a publication gate.
The sole maintainer can manually dispatch publication from main without a separate approval environment or receipt.
The direct workflow uses the configured filename and environment OIDC identity without npm tokens or trust-inspection artifacts.
The controller, ceremony, rehearsal, recovery, and trust-inspection workflows are absent from the publication path.
